name: KATTER, the Hon. Robert (Bob) Carl

headline.note: Katter's Queensland Parliament oral history provides a strong first-person sequence of family retail and cinema work, university study, mining activity, Mount Isa Mines labouring, cattle ownership and an insurance agency before elected office. Official biographies corroborate the occupation categories but do not publish exact employment boundaries, legal entities, hours or leave. His Citizens Military Forces service was reserve service and is not assumed to be full-time. Elected office is excluded. No defensible public/private full-time total can yet be calculated; missing evidence is not zero.

career_spells.employer: Katter family clothing store and picture theatre, Cloncurry
career_spells.role: Clothing-store worker by day and picture-theatre worker by night
career_spells.evidence_note: In the Queensland Parliament oral history Katter says he worked in the family businesses for the best part of two years after boarding school and before university, working in the clothing store during the day and picture theatre at night for about 70 hours a week. The business legal entities and calendar dates are not supplied. State Library material independently locates Katter C.R. & Co. in Cloncurry in 1967 but does not establish Bob Katter's employment interval.
career_spells.counting_note: Substantive private work is supported, but exact boundaries and payroll or ownership status are unresolved.

career_spells.evidence_note: Katter says he attended university for six years before leaving without completing law. ABC corroborates that he was a university student by the Beatles' 1964 Australian tour. Attendance dates are not derived from these relative statements.

career_spells.employer: Australian Citizens Military Forces / 49th Battalion, Royal Queensland Regiment
career_spells.evidence_note: Official parliamentary material records service in the Citizens Military Forces from 1964 to 1972 and the rank of Second Lieutenant. This was reserve service; service days, remuneration, any full-time training periods and leave are not published.
career_spells.counting_note: Part-time reserve service is not counted without a defensible FTE fraction or documented full-time interval.

career_spells.employer: Self-directed mining venture / company (legal entity not identified)
career_spells.evidence_note: Katter says he returned home during a mining boom, was floating his own mining company and later brought the Flor Dora mine into production. Official biographies describe small mining interests. Legal entity, ownership share, dates, hours, income and continuity—including possible overlap with elected office—are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Self-employment may count when substantive full-time boundaries are supported; they are not here.

career_spells.evidence_note: The official biographies list labouring work. Katter's oral history specifically says he laboured in Mount Isa's lead smelter after the mining boom crashed, and ABC describes the work as unskilled mine labour. Appointment, cessation, shift pattern, leave and legal employing entity are not published.
career_spells.counting_note: The private employer and substantive labour are supported, but no bounded full-time interval is established.

career_spells.employer: Saint Francis station and other Gulf Country cattle interests
career_spells.evidence_note: Katter says he built a substantial beef herd and bought 250,000 acres without debt. In 2009 Hansard he identified the station as Saint Francis, said he owned 250,000 unencumbered acres when he entered parliament, and described having cattle in the Gulf Country throughout his adult life. Official biographies identify cattle interests and ABC describes him as a grazier. The legal ownership entity, acquisition date, operating hours, disposal or succession date and overlap with elected office remain unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Ownership alone is not treated as full-time employment, and the operating interval is unbounded.

career_spells.employer: AMP insurance agency operated by Katter; agency legal entity unidentified
career_spells.evidence_note: Katter identifies his agency as AMP in 2018 and 2020 Hansard, selling savings and superannuation contracts. In a 2017 first-person parliamentary account he says he worked hard to build a very large and lucrative business and that AMP agents assessed whether clients could sustain savings-plan repayments, with the agency at risk if defaults reached three per cent. This strengthens the evidence for substantive agency operation and client-affordability assessment, but does not identify the agency legal entity, exact appointment/cessation, workload, overlaps or AMP payroll status.
career_spells.counting_note: Private self-employment is supported but cannot be counted without full-time boundaries.

career_spells.role: Member for Flinders, including ministerial service
career_spells.evidence_note: The Queensland Parliament former-member register gives the Flinders service interval and documents Katter's ministerial offices. His personal-history page says he retired on 25 August 1992; the parliamentary term boundary is retained here and the discrepancy is noted for follow-up.
Official parliamentary service begins with election to the House of Representatives on 13 March 1993.
Official state biography names AWU;2013 Hansard recalls briefly representing a union in youth. Dates, paid status and overlap with mine labour unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Excluded category; not added to public/private employment headlines.

career_spells.employer: University of Queensland student union and student/college bodies
career_spells.role: Student union representative and faculty/college council officeholder
career_spells.evidence_note: Oral historypp1–2 describes three years in student union and faculty, St Leos and combined colleges leadership. Governance context; remuneration and boundaries unknown, no university payroll inferred.
career_spells.counting_note: Excluded category; not added to public/private employment headlines.

career_spells.evidence_note: Oral history recounts party office before parliamentary entry; dates/pay not established.
career_spells.counting_note: Excluded category; not added to public/private employment headlines.

career_spells.evidence_note: Oral history describes setting up local Young Christian Workers; no payroll or calendar dates established.
career_spells.counting_note: Excluded category; not added to public/private employment headlines.

career_spells.employer: Self / Murdoch Books Australia and New Holland (publishers)
career_spells.evidence_note: Books published2012 and2017; writing intervals, advances/royalties and hours unknown. Publishers are counterparties, not proven payroll employers. Activity overlaps elected office; publication dates not encoded as employment boundaries.
career_spells.counting_note: Dates, substantive full-time status and/or leave remain insufficiently evidenced; no headline years calculated.

research_notes: Identify the legal entities and exact calendar dates for the Katter family clothing store, picture theatre, mining company, Flor Dora mine, cattle property and insurance agency; determine ownership versus payroll status and substantive hours.
Obtain Mount Isa Mines personnel or archival evidence for appointment, cessation, legal employer, shifts and leave.
Resolve whether mining, cattle and insurance operations continued during Queensland or federal elected office; ownership or a declared interest is not automatically substantive employment.
Investigate the Australian Workers Union representative entry in the Queensland register: role, paid status, dates, employing body and overlap with mine labour.
Resolve any paid employment in the 19 September 1992 to 13 March 1993 inter-parliamentary interval and the state retirement-date discrepancy (25 August versus 19 September 1992).

2026-10-02 follow-up: AMP insurer identified through two first-person parliamentary speeches; AWU representative and author activities separated from ordinary employment. Student/community/party offices recorded without assuming pay. Re-read oral historypp1–2 and searched mining/Flor Dora, agency and publisher records; no exact employment boundaries or hours located. Army service of father Robert Cummin Katter and First Databank executive namesake excluded. Further leads: AMP historical agent directories; Mount Isa Mines payroll archives; local property/company records. Source403 at official profile/register recovered via indexed material and accessible Hansard. Family-business70-hour workload remains supported but calendar interval/pay basis unresolved; no totals calculated.

2026-10-03 follow-up: a 2017 first-person parliamentary account strengthens the AMP agency evidence by describing a large, lucrative business and the agent's client-affordability/default-assessment responsibility. It still supplies no appointment or cessation date, weekly hours, legal agency entity, AMP payroll status or overlap boundaries. Fresh searches for Mount Isa Mines personnel, Flor Dora mining records, cattle-property identity and AMP directories did not resolve those gaps; no duration calculated.

2026-10-04 follow-up: 2009 Hansard identifies the cattle property as Saint Francis station and says Katter owned 250,000 unencumbered Gulf Country acres when he entered parliament; this materially improves property identity and supplies a December 1974 ownership observation but does not prove a full-time operating interval. Searches of Queensland Parliament, Trove, APH/OpenAustralia and mining/insurance terms otherwise repeated the oral-history sequence and supplied no Mount Isa Mines personnel boundary, AMP agency entity or appointment dates, Flor Dora legal entity, mining dates, hours or 1992–1993 employment. Revisit historical land/company titles, AMP agent directories and Mount Isa Mines archives.
